recipes.name: Feta and Bacon Stuffed Chicken with Onion Mashed Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 0.75 pound bacon, cut into 1 inch pieces
3 (4 ounce) skinless, boneless chicken breast halves

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Place bacon in a large, deep skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned but still soft, 5 to 7 minutes. Cool bacon on a paper towel-lined plate; reserve grease in the skillet.
Mix together cooled bacon with feta cheese, 3 tablespoons sour cream, oregano, and black pepper in a small bowl until well combined; set aside.
Lay chicken breasts flat on a clean work surface. Use the tip of a sharp boning or paring knife to cut a 2-inch pocket in each chicken breast. Spoon bacon mixture into the pockets.

Place flour, bread crumbs, and beaten eggs into separate, shallow dishes. Dredge a chicken breast in flour; shake off excess. Dip into beaten eggs. Lift up so excess egg drips back into the dish. Press into bread crumbs to coat both sides. Repeat with remaining chicken breasts.

Reheat grease in the skillet over medium heat. Sear chicken breasts in the hot grease until browned on both sides, about 2 minutes per side. Reserve grease in the skillet. Transfer chicken breasts to a baking dish.

Bake in the preheated oven until chicken is no longer pink and filling is hot, 20 to 25 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).
Meanwhile, place potatoes into a large pot and cover with salted water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain.
While potatoes are cooking, cook and stir onion in remaining grease in the skillet over medium heat until very tender and golden brown, about 10 minutes.
Place cooked potatoes into a large bowl. Add onion, remaining 3 tablespoons sour cream, and butter; mix well. Serve alongside stuffed chicken breasts.

raw_recipe.headline: Feta and Bacon Stuffed Chicken with Onion Mashed Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: This stuffed chicken with mashed potatoes features a rich and savory feta and bacon filling that is sure to impress guests at your next dinner party!

review.reviewBody: Good grief people! You are supposed to rate the recipe on HOW IT TASTES not on how the picture looks or how many calories are in it or the ingredients you THINK should have been included. If you haven't eaten it please don't make the rest of scroll through useless reviews to find helpful ones!

Loved the flavor combinations. I never have luck with stuffed chicken, so I filleted, breaded, and seared the chicken first, then piled the filling on top of each piece, covered, and baked. I also added two minced cloves of fresh garlic and a cup of mozzarella cheese to the mix. Served it with brown rice and peas to make up for the extra calories. Everyone loved it!

I made this with a slow cooker loaded baked potato soup with the consistency of a slightly runnier baked potato instead of the onion potato mix in the recipe and the family was good with it. We got some picky eaters around here so, yeah, 5 star

awesome receipe, the only thing I did different was the patotoes I sautéed them with onions and green beans and a little bit of bacon on the stove. I did add fresh garlic and fresh dried red pepper flakes to the stuffing for the chicken but everything else stayed the same.

This was the first time I've ever made stuffed chicken breasts, I suggest with this recipe you do as I did, and prep the day before by cooking the bacon and mixing it with the feta and other ingredients. Cut up and saute the onions and the potatoes too. Just add water and a couple table spoons of lemon juice to the potatoes to prevent them from turning brown and store them in a sealed bowl. Also store the Feta mix and onions is seperate sealed bowls as well. Be sure to drain the drippings from the bacon into a container while still liquified in the pan.

Prepping the chicken and frying it is enough work in itself on the day you plan on serving this dish. I only served it for the four of us and feel as though prep time for a rookie can be almost up to an hour. So just be prepared and leave yourself enough time.

Be sure to have extra breadcrumbs on hand depending on the size of the chicken breasts you may need more. I also seasoned the chicken lightly with Garlic Salt, Old Bay Seasoning, and black pepper and dried oregano.

When the potatoes are done heat the sauted onions in the microwave for 30 seconds so the mixture softens and isn't cold when adding to the potatoes to mash them.

I made it with 2 minor changes. I only had precooked bacon so I crumbled that in olive oil to heat and flavor the oil and then added it to the sour cream mixture. I also used small golden potatoes and left the skin on. Everything else was followed exactly. It was devoured and I will certainly make again. 4 stars due to minor changes I had to make with ingredients on hand

Yum, I only made a slight detour from the original recipe...pan fried the bacon, and used cornflake crumbs instead of bread crumbs. The chicken was moist and flavourful. I don't think I stuffed it enough, I had 5 breasts and was left over with some of the bacon/cheese mixture. I used it in scrambled eggs the next day. Will make again, but not too often just because of high caloric intake, but delicious!
I subtracted the bacon and served this with a romaine and orange(sprinkled with cinnamon) salad; using fresh squeezed orange juice as the salad dressing. It was delicious and much healthier.

First off, unless you have a sous-chef, prep time of 15 minutes is NOT possible. The total time from start to finish was about 2 hours. And I'm fast in the kitchen! Aside from that it was not hard to make and was tasty. I used whole chicken breasts, which is what added to the total time. It took about 50 minutes to get them up to temp at 350. So, adjust accordingly. I would not use the whole breast next time as the family all said it was A LOT of chicken. Half a breast of chicken per "pocket" would have been good for a single serving per person. I doubled the recipe but think 1.5 Lbs of bacon would have been too much. I used 3/4 Lb in the chicken and added the final 1/4 lb to the potatoes. Overall, it was tasty. The feta added the right amount of salt to the dish, so do not add any extra.

This was a hit!! I used reduced fat Feta cheese, 1 tablespoon of oregano, and crackers mixed with garlic salt instead of breadcrumbs. I baked it in a 9X13 pan for 45 minutes in the oven instead of frying the chicken.

Turned out well , although i tweaked a little for my tastes. I added minced pepperoni and made sure the Feta cheese was crumbled really well to begin with into the mix. I also made a light white wine garlic cream sauce to enhance the presentation.
Added Montreal steak spice to bread crumbs, no other changes. Cooked for 40 minutes
We really enjoyed this recipe! Only thing I changed, just dipped chicken in egg then seasoned Panko crumbs (seasoned the crumbs). We loved the stuffing & will definitely make again!

This is delicious. The only reason I’m giving the recipe 4 instead of 5 stars is that you will in all likelihood need to play around with the recipe more so than with your average recipe. I might suggest making it as written and going from there. Thank you for the recipe!

I thought it tasted fine. The chicken breasts, because of their size, came out SUPER tender. I wasn't as impressed with the feta as I thought I would be. And I LOVE feta! But, for ME, I prefer the taste of cream cheese and will probably make this the next time with cream cheese.
This is an excellent meal. I did change it up a bit and smoked my breast without the breaded outer crust. I used some Texas Oil Dust seasoning that I love. It was amazing!

Not really adept at stuffing (except my mouth☺), but went ahead and gave it a go. I was quite pleased with the flavor. I need a formal like recipe dish and this will work. I enjoyed the onion smashed potatoes (did add some left over bacon into the potatoes, cause one cannot ever have enough bacon. Thanks for a delicious recipe. Keep experimenting, you are onto something.

This was very good. It makes a GENEROUS amount of feta/bacon stuffing. I had quite a bit left over. I think next time I’ll reduce both the bacon amount and the feta amount. One question…. What is 1/8 Tbsp? I’m sure it’s a misprint in the recipe. I like oregano so I used 1/4 tsp and the taste was good. The onion amount could be decreased just a bit for the potatoes, but they were very good. I will definitely make this recipe again with my own little tweaks.
All I can say is... OMG! Delicious! Moist, flavorful; most definitely not for anyone watching their diet but so worth the calories and fat!
